about.account: Accounts are optional. When you sign in, your browser derives two keys from your password with PBKDF2 (600,000 rounds): one to sign in, and a vault key that never leaves the browser. Your list of notes (titles, keys, admin links) is encrypted with that vault key.
about.append: Visitors can only add lines below. Good for attendance, idea boards, report logs.
about.blocks: Type /spoiler for a block that opens on click, or /pin for a block encrypted again with a PIN. Handy for answer keys or credentials in the middle of an ordinary document.
about.burn: A note can delete itself after being opened 1, 3 or 10 times, or after a set time. Readers press a button first, so link previews in WhatsApp, Telegram or Slack don't use up a view. Opening it with the admin link doesn't count.
about.check: The text is locked, but - [ ] checkboxes can be ticked. For shopping lists or team runbooks.
about.edit: Anyone with the link can change it. Save conflicts are detected, so nothing is silently overwritten.
about.eyebrow: The server stores your notes but can't read them
about.freeze: Freeze version makes a permanent copy of the note as it is right now, with a read-only link nobody can change, not even you. The original stays editable as your next draft.
about.lead: Notes are encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM before they're sent. The key lives after the # in the link, and browsers never send that part to any server.
about.limit1: Anyone holding the full link can read the note. Treat the link like its password.
about.limit2: Images from other sites aren't loaded, so readers don't leak to third parties.
about.limit3: Checklist ticks and the number of additions are visible to the server, but their content isn't.
about.links_p: One note can have many links with different permissions: say, an edit link for your team and a read-only link for a client. The server enforces them, and every change must also prove the sender holds the note key.
about.raw1: Public notes (encryption off) can be fetched as plain text:
about.raw2: Encrypted notes can't be read through /raw: the server doesn't have the key.
about.s1t: The text only exists in this tab.
about.s2t: A random 256-bit key, plus a password if you set one.
about.s3t: Plus the link rules: mode, expiry, burn after reading.
about.s4t: The link /n/abc#k=… unlocks it in their browser.
about.timed: A time capsule keeps the content on the server until a set time; readers see a countdown. A scheduled lock turns edit, append and checklist links read-only at a set time, for sign-up lists or forms with a deadline.
